season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is rehabbing ACL/knee surgery and is on track for Week 1 vs Denver, so in a 6-pt passing TD league he is a discounted elite if the knee holds, with newly signed Kenneth Walker III soaking up Chiefs goal-line work either way.

Four unresolved QB battles - Cousins vs rookie Fernando Mendoza (LV), Kyler Murray vs J.J. McCarthy (MIN), Deshaun Watson vs Shedeur Sanders/Dillon Gabriel (CLE), Tua Tagovailoa vs Michael Penix Jr. (ATL) - suppress every attached pass-catcher until named, and Murray is the one whose rushing floor changes a fantasy outcome most in this scoring.

Miami executed a full teardown - Tua released to Atlanta, Jaylen Waddle traded to Denver, Tyreek Hill released - leaving a 4.5 win total, so avoid Dolphins offense entirely and target the Miami matchup for opposing DSTs.

A.J. Brown was traded to New England and Romeo Doubs signed there too, giving Drake Maye a real WR corps coming off a Super Bowl LX run, while in Philadelphia the vacated alpha targets consolidate TD equity onto Saquon Barkley, Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith.

Roughly 21 of 32 teams have new offensive coordinators and 10 have new head coaches, so early-season scheme variance is extreme and stable environments like Cincinnati, Green Bay and Houston carry a reliability premium.

Malik Nabers had a spring follow-up procedure on the knee he tore in Week 4 last year and the Giants under new HC John Harbaugh will be cautious, making his early-round price a trap despite the talent.

Sam LaPorta is coming off lower-back microdiscectomy on a roughly 10-month window to Week 1 with load management likely, which spikes Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs target/TD equity in Detroit (verify timeline).

Chicago vacated about 150 targets by trading DJ Moore to Buffalo, and second-year Ben Johnson play-calling funnels that to Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and TE Colston Loveland - Burden's elite rookie 2.92 YPRR makes him the priority in a yardage-and-TD league.

Rookie RB Jeremiyah Love went third overall to Arizona and every recent top-12-drafted RB has finished top-12 in fantasy, but the Cardinals' 4.5 win total caps his TD environment, making him volume-safe yet ceiling-limited.

Betting markets set Baltimore at a board-high 11.5 wins under new HC Jesse Minter and have Cincinnati favored in 15 games with a bottom-3 defense, marking BAL and CIN as the shootout/TD environments to stack.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur with OC Nathaniel Hackett rebuilt around No. 3 pick RB Jeremiyah Love, but a 4.5 win total means Trey McBride target volume and Love touches are safe while everyone else is TD-starved.
Kevin Stefanski takes over with an unsettled Tua-vs-Penix QB battle, so Bijan Robinson's volume is the only bankable asset and Drake London/Kyle Pitts prices should wait for a named starter.

New HC Jesse Minter handed the offense to first-time play-caller Declan Doyle; Lamar Jackson's rushing keeps him elite in this scoring, but thin WR depth behind Zay Flowers and a declining Mark Andrews add variance.

New HC Joe Brady and OC Pete Carmichael keep Josh Allen a 6-pt-TD monster, but acquired DJ Moore is on a three-year efficiency decline at 29 and Buffalo's slow pace caps secondary pieces - James Cook's TD role is the second-best asset.

Dave Canales runs it back but RT Taylor Moton's lung blood clot guts the line, and the Chuba Hubbard (3.8 post-injury YPC) vs Jonathon Brooks (two ACL tears, now cleared) backfield is a cheap-side-only investment.
Year-2 Ben Johnson with Caleb Williams and ~150 vacated targets after the DJ Moore trade makes Luther Burden the breakout bet, Odunze the deep-ball TD play, and Loveland a sneaky TE1.
Continuity with Zac Taylor plus a 29th-to-32nd-ranked defense means forced shootouts; Burrow (healthy), Chase, Higgins and Chase Brown are all pay-up environments in a TD-and-yardage league.

New HC Todd Monken inherits an open Watson-vs-Shedeur Sanders QB competition and traded Myles Garrett away, so TE Harold Fannin's 21% target share is the only near-safe piece and the DST loses its engine.
Schottenheimer year 2 leans on Javonte Williams' volume after an RB11 finish, but his league-worst receiving efficiency and Jaydon Blue's speed make him a TD-dependent hold at an inflated price.
Sean Payton traded for Jaylen Waddle to pair with year-3 Bo Nix, but Waddle needs route condensing (only 376 routes last year) to hit WR1 - a classic Payton efficiency-over-volume situation.

Dan Campbell imported OC Drew Petzing while Sam LaPorta rehabs back surgery, tilting early-season TD equity toward Gibbs, Montgomery-replacement work and Jameson Williams deep shots (verify RB2 role).

Rare continuity with LaFleur/Stenavich, and Doubs plus Wicks leaving condenses routes onto Christian Watson (elite 2.2+ YPRR deep threat, ideal non-PPR), Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden (verify Golden's role).

DeMeco Ryans kept OC Nick Caley, upgraded the O-line and added veteran RB help, so C.J. Stroud rebounds while rookie-year riser Jayden Higgins pushes past 29-year-old David Montgomery-style aging pieces for TD share (verify backfield mix).

Shane Steichen continuity makes TE Tyler Warren (21.2% rookie target share) the centerpiece with Michael Pittman's targets vacated and Alec Pierce coming off ankle surgery; slot-only Josh Downs is devalued in non-PPR.
Liam Coen year 2 hands the backfield to Bhayshul Tuten (7 TDs on 93 touches, 31% missed-tackle rate) after Travis Etienne's exit - a clear-path RB with the elusiveness profile this scoring pays for.

Andy Reid brought Eric Bieniemy back as OC, Mahomes tracks toward Week 1 off knee surgery, Kenneth Walker III signed for three years as the lead back, and Travis Kelce returns for year 14 - the TD engine is discounted, not dead.

Jim Harbaugh hired Mike McDaniel as OC, and that space-and-speed scheme is exactly what makes Omarion Hampton (RB3 overall in a week before his ankle injury) a top-10 upside back with Herbert a quiet 6-pt-TD value.

McVay promoted Nate Scheelhaase to OC and traded for Myles Garrett (DST surge), but 38-year-old Stafford is extraordinarily unlikely to repeat a 46-TD career year - buy the DST, fade the passing regression.

New HC Klint Kubiak opened camp with Kirk Cousins as QB1 over top rookie Fernando Mendoza, keeping the offense conservative; Ashton Jeanty's year-2 leap behind improved blocking is the one asset worth paying for on a 5.5-win team.
New HC Jeff Hafley and OC Bobby Slowik inherit a roster stripped of Tua, Waddle and Hill with a league-low-tier 4.5 win total - avoid the offense wholesale and stream DSTs against them.

Kevin O'Connell is splitting first-team reps between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy; Justin Jefferson is matchup-proof regardless, and a Murray win would add the rushing-QB ceiling this scoring format rewards.
Vrabel and McDaniels loaded a Super Bowl LX runner-up with A.J. Brown (via trade) and Romeo Doubs, making Drake Maye a top-tier 6-pt-TD bet and Brown a locked-in alpha with ~9-TD projection.

Kellen Moore's offense ascends around Tyler Shough, who closed last season with six 17-plus-point games and a 22.2% share of carries inside the 10 - rushing TD equity that plays up here - plus added weapons Jordyn Tyson and Travis Etienne (verify Etienne).

John Harbaugh's arrival brings a run-first, defense-led identity; Malik Nabers' knee (spring follow-up procedure) makes him a fade at cost, and the passing volume likely contracts for everyone (verify QB plan).

Aaron Glenn hired Frank Reich as OC for a structured reset, but 32-year-old Davante Adams-type veteran name value outpaces remaining juice and the offense projects bottom-quartile on a 5.5 win total (verify Adams role).

Sirianni with new OC Sean Mannion post-A.J. Brown-trade concentrates TD equity on Hurts' legs, Saquon Barkley's goal-line monopoly and DeVonta Smith's target dominance - fewer mouths, same 10.5-win offense.
Mike McCarthy takes over with a reworked staff and an unsettled QB plan, so Steelers skill players are TD-dependent bets until camp names a starter and a hierarchy (verify QB situation).

Shanahan (fine after an offseason car crash) signed Mike Evans for red-zone gravity, but Christian McCaffrey's 450-touch 2025 is the classic workload-cliff profile - pay for the offense, not the odometer.

The defending champs lost OC Klint Kubiak and RB Kenneth Walker III, promoting Brian Fleury and elevating Zach Charbonnet/Jadarian Price in the backfield; JSN stays elite and the DST remains a set-and-forget top unit (verify backfield split).

Todd Bowles hired Zac Robinson as OC, Mike Evans and Rachaad White are gone, and that hands Emeka Egbuka clear alpha targets and Kenny Gainwell (13.3 touches, 17.8 ppg from Week 8 on) a startable lead role.
Robert Saleh brought Brian Daboll to call plays for year-2 Cam Ward with pro-ready rookie WR Carnell Tate added - a quietly rising passing environment on a cheap 6.5 win total.
Dan Quinn continuity keeps Jayden Daniels a premium asset in a 6-pt passing TD plus rushing format, with a new OC in David Blough the main scheme question (verify play-caller impact).

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel now runs the Chargers offense and Hampton flashed RB3-overall weeks before his ankle injury; healthy with a scheme built for space, his yardage-plus-TD profile is top-10 upside.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Ben Johnson's offense vacated ~150 targets via the DJ Moore trade and Burden's 2.92 rookie YPRR sits with all-time breakout comps (Nacua, Chase, Jefferson) - yardage efficiency that pays directly in this scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans left for San Francisco, making Egbuka (68-938-6 as a rookie with four 20-plus-point games) the undisputed alpha for aggressive downfield thrower Baker Mayfield.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Travis Etienne's exit clears the Jacksonville backfield for Tuten, who scored 7 TDs on just 93 touches with a 31% missed-tackle rate - efficiency begging for volume.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Ranked dead last in yards before contact as a rookie yet still posted a 31.8-point game; improved Raiders blocking and a veteran QB stabilizer make the year-2 leap the bet.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: Third overall pick to Arizona with three-down skills, and every recent top-12-drafted RB finished top-12; the offense caps TDs but the volume floor is immediate.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Matched Nico Collins with 6 TDs as a rookie, produced when Collins sat, and Christian Kirk's departure opens perimeter routes in a rebounding Stroud offense - a TD-per-target riser, not a catch compiler.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Warren
breakout_watch.why: A 21.2% rookie target share plus Pittman's vacated 21% and Pierce's ankle rehab make Warren the Colts' target hub - TE1 overall upside at a discount.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six 17-plus-point games to close last season and 22.2% of Saints carries inside the 10 - goal-line QB rushing converts straight to 6-pt TDs in this format, with new weapons arriving.

breakout_watch.name: Christian Watson
breakout_watch.why: Doubs and Wicks left Green Bay, condensing routes onto a career 2.2-plus YPRR vertical threat; deep-ball yardage and TDs beat slot volume in non-PPR, health is the only gate.

breakout_watch.name: Jonathon Brooks
breakout_watch.why: Cleared after two ACL tears with Canales publicly praising him, facing only a 3.8-YPC post-injury Hubbard - an 11th/12th-round price on a possible lead job (verify camp reps).

breakout_watch.name: Kenny Gainwell
breakout_watch.why: Averaged 13.3 touches and 17.8 ppg from Week 8 on and Rachaad White departed - a cheap lead-back role in an improving Bucs offense.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Spring follow-up procedure on the Week 4 knee tear plus a new run-first Harbaugh regime - early-round price for a player likely managed cautiously into the season.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off a ~450-touch season at 30; the historical post-mega-workload cliff is near-universal, and his receiving value is muted in zero-PPR anyway.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age-38 season after a career-high 46-TD year - textbook TD regression, and -2 INTs bite harder if the arm slips.

fade_watch.name: DJ Moore
fade_watch.why: Three straight years of efficiency decline at 29, now in a Buffalo committee that spreads targets - catch volume without TD equity is worthless in this scoring.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: 2,100-plus career touches at 28 with efficiency down to 4.0 YPC and a late-season fade from 19.6 to 11.3 ppg - the volume is aging out (verify current depth chart).

fade_watch.name: Davante Adams
fade_watch.why: Age-32 with a declining production trajectory in a bottom-tier offense - name-brand ADP, contested-catch TDs are the only path (verify team context).

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: 3.8 YPC since his injury and Jonathon Brooks cleared and pushing - a timeshare masquerading as a starter price.

fade_watch.name: David Montgomery
fade_watch.why: Age-29, year 8, opportunities already fell from 17.4 to 11 per game - only 8-plus goal-line TDs saves the pick, which is a thin thesis.

fade_watch.name: Sam LaPorta
fade_watch.why: Lower-back microdiscectomy with load management expected - paying a top-TE price for a partial early season is negative EV.

fade_watch.name: Derrick Henry
fade_watch.why: Age-32 with historic career workload and consensus decline projections - the TD totals that carried him regress before the ADP does.

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled right now: four open QB battles (LV, MIN, CLE, ATL) that won't resolve until preseason reps, Mahomes' Week 1 knee status, Nabers and LaPorta recovery timelines, and several post-trade depth charts (Seattle and Detroit backfields, Houston RB mix, Green Bay WR pecking order); camp practices just opened July 28 so role reporting is one week old at best, and items tagged (verify) reflect single-source claims.
